about: Inputs of derive.py (pr-s33a-setting-far-field.md section 5.3). Every number carries its source. Scene frame: metres, +x east, +z south, the lane's centre the origin; true north is -z (step-33 SD-S33-1, pr-s33a section 5.1).

constants.source: RL-b C8's method (pr-rl-b-3d-budget.md:204-205, 619-630): elevation angle (h - h_eye - d^2 (1 - k) / (2 R)) / d, R 6 371 km, k 0.13 (Gauss, via Hirt et al. 2010, JGR 115 D21102); eye height 1.66 m (the slice's EYE0)

lake.source: USGS National Hydrography Dataset, Waterbody - Large Scale (layer 12), the National Map's ArcGIS REST service hydro.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nhd/MapServer

site_rule.land_source: (d), a bounded addition at C2 (recorded in SOURCE.md and the design's ledger for the Opus review): the village stands north of the lane, so no NHD water within 50 m on the northern half (270-90 deg). The scene's northern places reach 23 m (the cottage rows) and the platform's north end 44 m from the origin (step-33 section 4.0; pr-s33d section 5.5). Without it, rule 3 chose r0-01900, a point with water 40 m to its north on 280-30 deg
site_rule.source: pr-s33a section 5.2: candidates 20 m inland of the north shoreline every 50 m; (a) water on 150-210 deg out to 300 m; (b) no land rises within reach_m (80 m) on 120-240 deg; (c) Cuyamaca Peak's crest angle clears the highest sample on its ray inside 4 km by 0.3 deg; then the shoreline closest to east-west, ties by the longer water extent along 180 deg. water_from_m 40 skips the 20 m inland offset and a 20 m shore band; rise_tolerance_m 3.0 is this tool's reading of 'no land rises' (approximate; the C2 review confirms it)

summits.name: Cuyamaca Peak
summits.height_source: NGS 'Cuyamaca reset', the RL-b summit table (pr-rl-b-3d-budget.md:619-630; reverted skyline.gd SUMMITS :77)
summits.position_source: NGS 'Cuyamaca reset' as recorded in RL-b's table (58bc0c4 skyline.gd:77)

pointer.source: pointer only: the Wikipedia infobox (5 730 ft, after Peakbagger); the GNIS geonames service lists no summit of this name (cache/gnis.json)

summit_rule: A summit marked pointer takes the highest USGS 3DEP sample of a grid round a pointer coordinate (a secondary source used only to find the place); its position and height are 3DEP's. A summit marked gnis takes its coordinate from the USGS GNIS (the National Map geonames service, layer 5 Landforms, class Summit, cached in cache/gnis.json with its gaz_id) and its height from USGS 3DEP at that coordinate (EPQS, cached in cache/epqs.json). A summit GNIS does not list is reported as missing, never invented

places.about: Floor rectangles in the scene frame (x east, z south, metres), translated by step-33 section 4.0 and pr-s33c section 5.5: lane (x, y) mm -> scene (x/1000 - 15, 3 - y/1000)

pier.source: pr-s33b-lakeside-bodies.md section 5.3 (FROZEN): the pier's lane-frame footprint x 16 000-20 000, y -20 000-0

station.source: pr-s29a-town-contract.md rev. 3, Lakeside's halt table: station here (400, 2500), lane there (29600, 3000), 8 x 5 m; floor = floor + (there - here) +/- 800 across the wall (pr-s33b section 5.1)

station-platform.source: pr-s29a-town-contract.md rev. 3: station-platform here (-3600, -16000), station there (7600, 2500), floor x -4 000-0, y -20 000-20 000, track on the east edge (Q-S29a-7)
